clue.text: Management of bed onboard delivered in French letter?

indicators.note: a speech is delivered out loud, so we want a word that is heard rather than seen

blocks.note: a berth is a bed on a ship; the spoken word gives a same-sounding spelling
management of something is control of it

explanation.surface: Someone asks how to manage a bed on a ship, delivered in a letter written in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Management of X' gives X CONTROL, so the sounded-out berth comes first. 'Delivered' also hints at childbirth, a double layer of misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A French letter is old British slang for a condom, which is one example of contraception; the question mark flags definition by example.

clue.text: Houses listening devices picking up long row after lunchtime?

indicators.note: to pick something up is to take it inside, so one piece is held within another
placing one thing after another tells us which piece comes second in the chain

blocks.note: bugs are hidden microphones
lunch is at one o'clock, and one is I in Roman numerals
L is the dictionary abbreviation for long
a row is a loud noise, a din

explanation.surface: Surveillance devices in houses pick up a long argument that starts after lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' here rhymes with 'cow', a racket. The I and L-DIN chain sits inside BUGS: BU-ILDIN-GS.
explanation.definitionFit: Houses are a kind of structure people live in, so they are examples of buildings; the plural noun matches.

clue.text: S. Connery was one raised to put away German dishes

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising letters lifts them from bottom to top, running them backwards
putting something away means stowing it inside, so one piece goes into another

blocks.note: the initial taken as written
Sean Connery was knighted, so he was a Sir
Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: Sean Connery, once raised to the knighthood, puts away plates of German food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'S. Connery' reads as a name, but the initial is a letter in its own right and 'was one' points to his title; the lifted pair then swallows the German.
explanation.definitionFit: A risotto is an Italian rice dish, so the plural is several such meals, a straightforward example of dishes.

clue.text: Book hotel over by expanse of water

blocks.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
a sea is a large expanse of water

explanation.surface: An instruction to reserve a hotel overlooking the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb meaning reserve; it is the noun. An over in cricket is a set of six balls, abbreviated O.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosea is one of the minor prophets and a book of the Old Testament, so it is one example of a Bible book.

clue.text: Design proves I will get surplus

indicators.note: to design something is to plan and shape it anew, so the letters are given a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
I will contracts to I'll; the apostrophe is ignored

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that their design work will earn them a surplus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Design' reads as a noun subject; it is an imperative telling you to rework the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Overspill is the excess that flows over when there is too much, so it is a synonym of a surplus or excess.

clue.text: Fruit, say 2 x 2 ÷ (1000 + 1)

indicators.note: 'say' asks us to speak the figure, taking the word it sounds like rather than its digit
the multiplication sign means times, so the same spoken figure is used twice in the chain
a division sign splits a thing in two, so the pair is parted with something put between

blocks.note: the number spoken sounds like the little preposition
M is a thousand in Roman numerals
one is 'a', as in a single thing
again the spoken number

explanation.surface: A sum written out like a maths homework problem, with the fruit as its answer.
explanation.walkthrough: '2 x 2' is two lots of the spoken number, and the division sign cuts them apart so that M+A sits in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically a tomato is a berry, the fleshy seed-bearing part of the plant, even though cooks treat it as a vegetable.

clue.text: Intermittently dotty, that woman’s different

indicators.note: something intermittent comes and goes, so we keep a letter, skip one, and keep the next

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters
her is the pronoun for that woman

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a woman who is now and then a bit mad is unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the even letters of dotty, then the pronoun. The 's in 'woman's' is 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Other and different are synonyms as adjectives: an other way is a different way, distinct from the one already named.

clue.text: King allegedly in ruins

indicators.note: something alleged is only what people say, so we go by the spoken sound of the word

blocks.note: Rex is Latin for king, as in royal signatures

explanation.surface: A monarch is said to be living among crumbling ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: REX is the crossword king, found after a sovereign's name on documents; said aloud it matches a word for destroyed things.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruins as a verb means destroys, and wrecks carries the same sense; as nouns both are remains of something smashed.

clue.text: Drivers keep an eye on this drug ring

definitions.text: Drivers keep an eye on this

blocks.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Motorists are warned to watch out for a narcotics gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drug ring' reads as a criminal gang, but the two words split into a drug and a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedo is informal British for the speedometer, the dashboard dial a motorist glances at to check how fast the car is going.

clue.text: Top Thunderbird character showers

indicators.note: to top is to cut off the head, as when topping a plant, so the opening letter is removed

blocks.note: Brains is the boy-genius engineer in the puppet TV series Thunderbirds

explanation.surface: The best character in Thunderbirds takes a shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective meaning best; it is a verb meaning behead. Thunderbirds is a 1960s British puppet adventure series.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, showers and rains both describe water falling from the sky, so one stands in for the other.

clue.text: Vessel of cooked meats hard to sample outside

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new order
one thing set outside another wraps around it as a shell

blocks.note: the five letters rearranged
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
to sample a drink is to sip it

explanation.surface: A pot of cooked meats that is hard to try from the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' tempts you toward a cooking pot to go with the meats; it is a ship. The reworked meats plus H sit inside SIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is any ship or boat, and a steamship is one kind, driven by steam engines; so it is an example.

clue.text: Some chatted occasionally about last piece of work

indicators.note: 'some' asks for only part of the words that follow, a run of letters taken from inside them
to turn about is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters across the word break

explanation.surface: People occasionally chatted about the final item they worked on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasionally' looks like an alternate-letters signal, but here it only supplies letters: read chATTED OCcasionally backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a codetta is a short closing passage, a small coda at the end of a section or composition, its final part.

clue.text: Release group regularly tries iron shackles

indicators.note: doing something regularly means at even intervals, so we keep letters at a steady spacing
shackles fasten round a prisoner, so one piece is locked inside another

blocks.note: a set is a group of things
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A gang attempts to free prisoners kept in iron chains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shackles' sits naturally beside 'iron' as a noun, but it is a verb: FE wraps the alternate letters of tries.
explanation.definitionFit: To release a prisoner or animal is to let it go, which is exactly to liberate it; both phrases are transitive verbs.

clue.text: Part of Egyptian religion to adore red top?

blocks.note: a red top is a British tabloid newspaper with a red masthead, such as The Sun
to adore is to worship

explanation.surface: Was adoring a red-topped crown or headdress part of the faith of ancient Egypt?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red top' suggests a pharaoh's crown; it is the British name for a mass-market tabloid paper. 'Adore red top' gives the verb and object in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Egyptians venerated the solar deity Ra, so devotion to the solar disc was a central element of their faith.

clue.text: Puffin decided to eat a fish egg

indicators.note: whatever eats takes food inside it, so one piece swallows the others

blocks.note: decided, as in a fixed or settled matter, is set
taken as written
a parr is a young salmon
an egg is O-shaped

explanation.surface: A puffin made up its mind to swallow a fish's egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish egg' reads as roe, which suits the bird's diet; split them and the fish is a young salmon and the egg is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea parrot is an old folk name for the puffin, earned by its large, brightly coloured, parrot-like bill.

clue.text: Ancient queen achieved nothing

blocks.note: to achieve something is to do it
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A queen of long ago who accomplished nothing in her reign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing' reads as the object of 'achieved', but it is a separate piece: the zero-shaped letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido was the legendary founder and ruler of Carthage, abandoned by Aeneas in Virgil's epic, so a monarch of antiquity.

clue.text: Ladies excited to embrace first romantics

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up and agitated, so the letters are jumbled
an embrace wraps arms around someone, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: the six letters reworked
first is written 1st, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: Excited women hug the first romantic men they meet.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled ladies wrap around 1ST, with the digit 1 standing for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic in the sense of a dreamer who believes in perfection is an idealist; both are plural nouns for such people.

clue.text: Charge at crumbling old city

indicators.note: something crumbling is falling apart, so the letters break up and reform

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An army attacks a ruined ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbling' suits an ancient ruin in the surface, but its job is to break up the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Carthage was an ancient Phoenician city in North Africa, destroyed by Rome, so it is an example of an ancient settlement.

clue.text: Times describes you and me as ‘engaged’

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw its outline, so one piece is drawn round another

blocks.note: times as in multiplication: three by four
us is the pronoun for you and me

explanation.surface: A newspaper announces that the two of us are to be married.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make Times look like the newspaper, whose announcements page reports engagements; it is the multiplication word.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone line or a person that is engaged is occupied and unavailable, the same sense as busy.

clue.text: Following difficulty standing up, I upset state funeral

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing upright means reading from the bottom up, so the letters go backwards
to upset something is to tip it over, so in a down clue it is turned upside down
following means coming after, which fixes the order of the chain

blocks.note: a rub is a snag, as in 'there's the rub'
taken as written
LA is the postal abbreviation for Louisiana

explanation.surface: Someone who has trouble standing gets upset at a state funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State funeral' looks like a fixed phrase, but 'state' belongs to the wordplay. Both reversals turn on the clue reading downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A burial is the interment of a body, the central ceremony of a funeral, so the two nouns stand in for each other.

clue.text: Even drunk’s bored by final word of political body

indicators.note: being bored by something means being drilled through, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: on a par means even or level
lit is slang for drunk
amen is the word that ends a prayer

explanation.surface: Even a drunk would be bored by a political body's final say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bored' suggests tedium; it means pierced. The 's in drunk's is 'is', and the drunk word is the one holding the prayer ending.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliament is a national legislative assembly, a group of elected politicians, so it is a kind of governing body.

clue.text: Go on about prize

indicators.note: turning about means facing the opposite way, so the letters are reversed

blocks.note: a go in a game is a turn
re means on or concerning, as in a memo heading

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep talking about a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go on' reads as one verb meaning to ramble; it splits into a noun and a preposition. The Turner Prize is a prominent British contemporary art award.
explanation.definitionFit: The Turner Prize, named after the painter J. M. W. Turner, is awarded each year to a British visual artist.

clue.text: 150 tuck into boiled rice and get wind

indicators.note: to tuck something in is to slip it inside, so one piece goes within another
boiling makes things churn about, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: the four letters reworked
C is 100 and L is 50 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Eating a big plate of boiled rice gives 150 people indigestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get wind' suggests flatulence, but 'wind' is a verb rhyming with 'find'. 'Tuck into' looks like eating heartily; here it inserts.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind round something, like a path round a hill, is to go round it in a curve, which is to circle it.

clue.text: Duplicate sorted parcel I collected

indicators.note: sorting things puts them into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A second copy of a parcel I picked up from the sorting office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duplicate' could be a verb, but the answer is the noun. 'Collected' just reports the fodder gathered together.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact copy of an object, so it is a synonym of the noun duplicate.

clue.text: Calm tennis winner completes training

indicators.note: completing something means adding its final part, so this piece comes last

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
an ace is a serve the opponent cannot touch, winning the point

explanation.surface: A composed tennis champion finishes a training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tennis winner' points to a champion, but it means a winning shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm as a noun means stillness and quiet, which is a synonym of the noun naming tranquillity.

clue.text: Colonist, perhaps 25, secures lake

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: 25 across, Araucaria, was the pseudonym of a famous Guardian crossword compiler
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A colonist, maybe one who planted a monkey puzzle tree, claims a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference looks like it wants the tree, but Araucaria was John Graham's pen name as a setter, and 'perhaps' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonist is someone who moves to a new territory and makes a home there, which is what a settler does.

clue.text: John, in case of struggle, provides servant

indicators.note: a case is the outer shell around something, so only the outer letters are kept
'in' places one thing inside another

blocks.note: the first and last letters
john is slang for a toilet, and lav is a British word for one

explanation.surface: A man called John, caught in a fight, supplies a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: John reads as a person's name; it is American slang for a lavatory, whose short British form fits inside the outer pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A slave is a person forced to work without pay or freedom, the most extreme kind of servant.

clue.text: Fancy car with gold interior? Look – one reverses into tree

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or decorated, so the letters are dressed up in a new order
an interior is what lies inside, so one piece sits within another
to reverse is to go backwards, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: the three letters reworked
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
an air is a look or manner, as in 'an air of confidence'
one is 'a', a single thing

explanation.surface: Admiring a flashy gold-trimmed car, until it backs into a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads as an adjective for the car, but it rearranges it. 'Look' seems an exclamation; it is a noun meaning appearance, joined by A and turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Araucaria is the genus of conifers that includes the monkey puzzle tree, so it names a kind of tree.

clue.text: Sounds like I will shortly marry near here

indicators.note: 'sounds like' directly tells us to go by how a word is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: the short form of I will is the contraction

explanation.surface: Someone announces they will be getting married soon, nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' looks like 'soon' in the surface; it means the contracted form. The definition is cryptic: a church wedding happens beside this passage.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples walk up the central passageway of a church to the altar, so that is roughly where they wed.

clue.text: He lets nerves fray still

indicators.note: fraying rope comes apart into loose strands, so the letters unravel and reform

blocks.note: all three words taken as written

explanation.surface: A man lets his nerves fray even now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' sits at the end like an adverb of time for the fraying; it is the definition, meaning however.
explanation.definitionFit: As a sentence adverb, still means in spite of that, the same concessive sense as however or yet.
